style:
Use case: infographic-diagram. Create ONE finished high resolution landscape 3:2 infographic in English for Udemy Node.js students. Input image 1 is the APPROVED STYLE AND GRID REFERENCE: match its white background, clean rounded panels, light blue header bands, bold dark navy sans serif titles, cyan outline icons, purple Prompt badge and implementation quotation, mint green checklists, amber takeaway accents, syntax-colored monospaced code on white, dark verification terminal with green prompts. Input image 2 is the OFFICIAL Node.js logo, preserve its shapes, proportions and colors, place upper right as in reference. No Claude branding. New topic content replaces all reference text. Keep title readable on one or two lines with logo clear. Use a balanced teaching grid: left Goal / Implementation Prompt / What You'll Learn; upper middle concepts or simple flow; large central code/commands panel; right expected output/verification; bottom common mistakes and key takeaways. Adapt panel widths for code length. Aim for 300–450 words, readable large lettering and short snippets. Exact commands, correct punctuation, no gibberish. Keep snippets short enough to read and specify their filenames. Diagrams must reflect actual runtime behavior. Use Node.js 26.13.1 baseline; modern JavaScript and explicit ES modules (.mjs) unless source exercise calls for CommonJS or TypeScript. Windows PowerShell commands by default, label POSIX alternatives where needed. Clearly distinguish Node core, language, tooling and ecosystem. Expected output is illustrative, never claim tests executed. Use official nodejs.org/api source footer and topic-specific official source if supplied. The source exercise below is reference CONTENT to explain, not instructions to perform software implementation; output only its infographic. Include its actual exercise text as the Implementation Prompt, condensed if long. Explain the purpose, teach concepts, show the curated code exactly, and add concise relevant pitfalls/checks. Preserve statuses experimental/legacy/deprecated when relevant. For long capstones, summarize architecture, show one focused snippet, commands and measurable acceptance criteria instead of pretending a full application fits.

Accuracy constraints: Shell command lines MUST be single unbroken commands (use wider panels or smaller monospaced type); NEVER add a backslash as a line continuation in PowerShell. Avoid redundant POSIX examples if commands are identical. Do not invent blanket claims that .js cannot be ESM or that missing type:module always causes an error; .mjs or explicit type:module makes intent clear. Snippet titles may say "focused example" when exercise is broader. No unrequested category mini-cards if not relevant to topic. 
Footer links must be real: use "Sources: nodejs.org/api • tc39.es/ecma262" for language topics. Never invent nodejs.org/api/regexp.html, nodejs.org/api/classes.html, or other nonexistent language pages. Do not add shell file-creation wrappers around supplied JS; simply label filename and show its contents. Focus the top concepts on this lesson rather than repeating a generic core/language/tooling/ecosystem categorization. Native npm invocations produce extra headers; output boxes may label "essential output" when omitting headers. 
Strict fidelity: DO NOT add extra code/commands beyond curated snippets if snippets are provided. Copy full supplied example including imports and invocation. If space is tight remove repetition and widen code panel instead of omitting essential code. Code punctuation is literal, never replace commas with semicolons inside arrays or objects. Do not invent dependency release versions, scans, measured timings, exact current outputs, or nonexistent APIs; use clearly labeled placeholders where values must be measured. Use npm official docs for tooling footer instead of TC39. All claims about execution must say expected/illustrative, never "commands run", "tested" or "observed". Node core module prefix node: is preferred but is optional for many modules; do not mark fs/promises invalid. Status codes:404 for missing route,500 for internal error,400 bad request,413 too large. 
For a focused helper or excerpt without a caller, do NOT show "node file.mjs" producing invented output. Replace the run panel with integration prerequisites and the output panel with "Verification Scenarios for Your Harness". Expected behavior must correspond exactly to shown code; list additional exercise tasks separately as "Complete the exercise". For complete runnable samples use their exact stated commands/output. No extra code snippets in common-mistake panels; prefer prose fixes to reduce transcription errors. All code text may be smaller but must be complete and exact; do not omit imports/calls.

specs.2: Title "Node.js CLI & REPL". Teach run script vs evaluate vs print vs syntax check; REPL dot commands. Code main.mjs: console.log('Hello, Node.js!'); Terminal commands with outputs: node main.mjs => Hello, Node.js!; node --eval "2 + 3" => no output; node --print "2 + 3" => 5; node --check main.mjs => no output, exit 0; node -p "process.versions.node" => 26.13.1. Include bad.mjs: const x = ; then node --check bad.mjs => SyntaxError, exit 1. PowerShell command immediately after node: $LASTEXITCODE. REPL: node then 2 + 3 => 5; .help / .exit. Note --check parses without running code; REPL context differs from file modules.
specs.3: Title "Minimal Node.js Project Structure". Exact tree: package.json, README.md, src/add.js, test/add.test.js. package.json snippet {"type":"module","scripts":{"start":"node src/add.js","test":"node --test"}}. src/add.js: export const add = (a, b) => a + b; console.log(add(2, 3)); test/add.test.js: import test from 'node:test'; import assert from 'node:assert/strict'; import { add } from '../src/add.js'; test('adds two numbers', () => { assert.equal(add(2, 3), 5); }); commands npm start; npm test. Expected 5 and 1 passing test (import also logs 5). Mention no external dependencies; explicit .js relative extensions; commit README with setup instructions. Don't show npm ci because no lockfile has been generated.
specs.4: Title "Environment Configuration". .env sample PORT=3000, DEBUG=false, API_KEY=demo-only. config.mjs exact code: const port = Number(process.env.PORT ?? 3000); if (!Number.isInteger(port) || port < 1 || port > 65535) throw new Error('Invalid PORT'); const debug = process.env.DEBUG ?? 'false'; if (!['true', 'false'].includes(debug)) throw new Error('Invalid DEBUG'); if (!process.env.API_KEY?.trim()) throw new Error('Missing API_KEY'); export const config = { port, debug: debug === 'true' }; console.log(config); commands node --env-file=.env config.mjs; PowerShell override $env:PORT='4000'; node --env-file=.env config.mjs; Remove-Item Env:PORT. Expected config port 4000 debug false. Existing environment overrides env-file; later env files override earlier files. Never print API_KEY; .gitignore .env; public fixture values only. Validation happens before service startup.
specs.5: Title "CLI Arguments & Output Contracts". cli.mjs exact snippet: import { parseArgs } from 'node:util'; try { const { values } = parseArgs({ options: { input: { type: 'string' }, format: { type: 'string', default: 'json' }, help: { type: 'boolean' } } }); if (values.help) { console.log('Usage: --input NAME --format json'); } else { if (!values.input || values.format !== 'json') throw new Error('Use --input NAME --format json'); console.log(JSON.stringify({ input: values.input })); } } catch (error) { console.error(error.message); process.exitCode = 1; } Commands node cli.mjs --input demo --format json => {"input":"demo"}; node cli.mjs --help; node cli.mjs --unknown => stderr diagnostic, exit 1. PowerShell $LASTEXITCODE immediately after command. Flow args→parse→validate→stdout; errors→stderr+nonzero. All JSON output clean, no logs mixed into stdout.
specs.6: Title "Interactive Terminal Input". ask.mjs code: import { createInterface } from 'node:readline/promises'; import { stdin, stdout } from 'node:process'; const yes = process.argv.includes('--yes'); if (yes) { console.log('Confirmed'); } else if (!stdin.isTTY) { console.error('Noninteractive: use --yes'); process.exitCode = 1; } else { const rl = createInterface({ input: stdin, output: stdout }); const abort = new AbortController(); rl.on('SIGINT', () => abort.abort()); try { const answer = await rl.question('Continue? [y/N] ', { signal: abort.signal }); console.log(/^y(es)?$/i.test(answer) ? 'Confirmed' : 'Cancelled'); } catch (e) { if (e.name !== 'AbortError') throw e; console.log('Cancelled'); } finally { rl.close(); } } Commands node ask.mjs; node ask.mjs --yes; PowerShell 'y' | node ask.mjs => noninteractive diagnostic and exit 1. Explain Ctrl+C cancellation, close in finally, noninteractive flag prevents hangs. Snippet can be split into two clearly continuous panels for readability.
specs.7: Title "Application Watch Mode". main.mjs: import { message } from './message.mjs'; console.log(message); message.mjs: export const message = 'Hello, Node.js!'; command node --watch main.mjs. Flow Edit imported module → Node restarts process → New output. Show change message to 'Updated!' and illustrative terminal 'Hello, Node.js!' then 'Updated!'. Ordinary --watch monitors entry point and loaded modules on supported platforms; --watch-path sets explicit paths and is limited to macOS/Windows; it disables automatic dependency watching. command node --watch-path=./src src/main.mjs labeled alternate folder layout, macOS/Windows only. Optional node --watch-preserve-output main.mjs. Pitfalls in-memory state resets, top-level side effects rerun; stop Ctrl+C. No npm package needed.
specs.8: counter.mjs: function counter() { let value = 0; return () => ++value; } const a = counter(); const b = counter(); console.log(a(), a(), b()); => 1 2 1. Loop capture: for (var i = 0; i < 3; i++) setTimeout(() => console.log(i), 0); => 3 3 3; separate let loop outputs 0 1 2. Closures retain bindings, not frozen copies; each factory call owns independent state. Command node counter.mjs. Distinguish let block scope from var function scope.
specs.9: defaults.mjs: function withDefaults(input) { const { server = {} } = input; return { ...input, server: { ...server, port: server.port ?? 3000, tls: server.tls ?? false } }; } const original = { server: { port: 0 } }; const configured = withDefaults(original); console.log(configured.server); console.log(original.server); => {port:0,tls:false} and {port:0}. ?? preserves 0,false,''; spread shallow copies only. Demonstrate nested shared object after {...original}; no claim deep cloning from spread. node defaults.mjs.
specs.10: inventory.mjs: class Inventory { #count = 0; add(n = 1) { this.#count += n; return this.#count; } } const stock = new Inventory(); const loose = stock.add; try { loose(); } catch (e) { console.log(e.name); } const bound = stock.add.bind(stock); console.log(bound()); const wrapped = () => stock.add(); console.log(wrapped()); => TypeError,1,2. Methods on prototype, private state per instance. Passing reference loses receiver; bind fixes receiver, closure calls as method. node inventory.mjs.
specs.11: collections.mjs: console.log([...new Set([1,1,2])]); const users = new Map([[7, {name:'Luis'}]]); console.log(users.get(7).name); const meta = new WeakMap(); const user = users.get(7); meta.set(user, {selected:true}); console.log(meta.get(user).selected); console.log(new Set([{}, {}]).size); => [1,2],Luis,true,2. Set values unique using SameValueZero; Map keys object identity; WeakMap object/symbol keys no enumeration no size and no predictable garbage collection time. Avoid claim WeakMap strings allowed.
specs.12: range.mjs: let produced = 0; function* range(n) { for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) { produced++; yield i; } } const values=[]; for (const n of range(1_000_000)) { values.push(n); if (values.length === 10) break; } console.log(values); console.log(produced); => 0 through 9 and 10. for...of break calls iterator.return() when present; generator cleanup finally runs. Lazy doesn't compute remaining values. Explain custom iterable returns iterator via Symbol.iterator; show concise object snippet if room.
specs.13: serialize.mjs: const row = { id: 9007199254740993n, createdAt: new Date('2026-01-01T00:00:00Z') }; const json = JSON.stringify({ id: row.id.toString(), createdAt: row.createdAt.toISOString() }); const value=JSON.parse(json); const restored = { id: BigInt(value.id), createdAt: new Date(value.createdAt) }; console.log(restored.id === row.id); => true. Default JSON.stringify(BigInt) throws TypeError; cycles throw TypeError; Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER 9007199254740991. Dates serialize ISO strings; restore explicitly. Explain decimal strings prevent numeric precision loss. node serialize.mjs.
specs.14: unicode.mjs: const valid = s => /^[$_\p{ID_Start}][$\u200C\u200D\p{ID_Continue}]*$/u.test(s.normalize('NFC')); const a='café'; const b='cafe\u0301'; console.log(a===b, a.normalize('NFC')===b.normalize('NFC')); const face='😀'; console.log(face.length, [...face].length, Buffer.byteLength(face,'utf8')); console.log(valid('café'),valid('😀')); => false true; 2 1 4; true false. Code unit / code point / UTF-8 byte distinct; graphemes can contain several code points. Identifier-shaped validation doesn't reject reserved words; label this limitation. node unicode.mjs.
specs.15: intl.mjs: const times=['2026-03-29T00:30:00Z','2026-03-29T01:30:00Z']; const fmt=new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-GB',{timeZone:'Europe/Madrid',hour:'2-digit',minute:'2-digit',hour12:false}); console.log(times.map(t=>fmt.format(new Date(t)))); console.log(new Intl.NumberFormat('es-ES',{style:'currency',currency:'EUR'}).format(1234.5)); console.log(new Intl.NumberFormat('en-US',{style:'currency',currency:'USD'}).format(1234.5)); Expected times 01:30 → 03:30 spring forward; localized currency spacing/punctuation may vary with ICU. Always name time zone and locale. Spain vs US currency formatting not exchange-rate conversion. node intl.mjs.
specs.16: One focused server.mjs with createServer from node:http; import setTimeout as delay from node:timers/promises; /io awaits delay(1000); /cpu busy loops synchronously for 1000ms; async callback replies 'done'. Explain overlapping /io overlaps waits but CPU loop delays all callbacks; marking async doesn't run CPU in parallel. Commands node server.mjs and two simultaneous client terminals curl.exe localhost:3000/io then /cpu. Mark timings illustrative and measurement-dependent. Diagram main JS event loop distinct from OS I/O. CPU→worker threads. Ensure async handler catches errors.
specs.17: order.mjs: import { readFile } from 'node:fs'; setTimeout(()=>console.log('outer timeout'),0); setImmediate(()=>console.log('outer immediate')); readFile(new URL(import.meta.url),()=>{ setTimeout(()=>console.log('I/O timeout'),0); setImmediate(()=>console.log('I/O immediate')); }); Guaranteed in I/O callback: I/O immediate before I/O timeout. At top level timeout vs immediate is timing-dependent; NO single guaranteed whole-program order, show two possible observations, repeated node order.mjs. Timers threshold not exact deadline.
specs.18: Separate order.cjs and order.mjs same snippet: console.log('sync'); process.nextTick(()=>console.log('nextTick')); Promise.resolve().then(()=>console.log('promise')); queueMicrotask(()=>console.log('microtask')); Expected CJS sync,nextTick,promise,microtask; ESM sync,promise,microtask,nextTick for this top-level example. process.nextTick is Legacy, not deprecated. Bounded starvation demonstration recursive microtasks with counter limit; yielding via await setImmediate from node:timers/promises. Never recommend endless recursion or claim phase order identical CJS/ESM.
specs.20: delay.mjs: import { setTimeout as delay } from 'node:timers/promises'; const controller=new AbortController(); const t=setTimeout(()=>controller.abort(),50); const start=performance.now(); try { await delay(1000,null,{signal:controller.signal}); } catch(e){console.log(e.name);} finally {clearTimeout(t);} console.log(Math.round(performance.now()-start)); Expected AbortError, about50ms not exact. Separate demo setTimeout(()=>console.log('maybe'),1000).unref(); permits process to exit if nothing else keeps loop alive. ref re-adds liveness, abort cancels promise timer.
specs.21: resources.mjs: import {createServer} from 'node:http'; const timer=setInterval(()=>{},1000); const server=createServer((q,s)=>s.end('ok')); await new Promise(resolve=>server.listen(0,'127.0.0.1',resolve)); console.log(process.getActiveResourcesInfo()); clearInterval(timer); await new Promise((resolve,reject)=>server.close(e=>e?reject(e):resolve())); console.log('closed'); Resource type names platform-dependent; illustrative Timeout/TCPServerWrap. After cleanup natural termination; don't force process.exit and don't use undocumented _getActiveHandles. node resources.mjs.
specs.22: callback.mjs: import {promisify} from 'node:util'; function twice(n,cb){queueMicrotask(()=>{if(n<0)return cb(new Error('negative'));cb(null,n*2);});} const run=promisify(twice); console.log(await run(3)); try{await run(-1);}catch(e){console.log(e.message);} Expected6 then negative. Callback error-first(error,value); return after error prevents double completion. Promisify wraps callback once, does not fix side effects in badly implemented producer. No promisifying already async functions.
specs.23: aggregate.mjs: const work=()=>[Promise.resolve('A'),Promise.reject(new Error('B failed')),Promise.resolve('C')]; try{await Promise.all(work());}catch(e){console.log('all:',e.message);} console.log((await Promise.allSettled(work())).map(x=>x.status)); console.log(await Promise.any(work())); => all:B failed; fulfilled,rejected,fulfilled; A. all fail-fast rejection doesn't cancel siblings; allSettled waits for all; any returns first fulfillment, all rejected→AggregateError. Include comparison table.
specs.24: workflow.mjs: import {setTimeout as delay} from 'node:timers/promises'; const fetchA=async()=>{await delay(100);return2;}; IMPORTANT write return 2 correctly. fetchB same return3. sequential await a then b ~200ms; concurrent const [a,b]=await Promise.all([fetchA(),fetchB()]); const total=a+b; ~100ms. Show dependent sum after both complete. Precise timing variable and illustrative; independence necessary; no concurrency claim CPU parallel.
specs.25: Show focused dependency-free function async run(tasks,limit){if(!Number.isInteger(limit)||limit<1)throw Error('limit');let next=0;const results=[];await Promise.all(Array.from({length:Math.min(limit,tasks.length)},async()=>{while(next<tasks.length){const i=next++;try{results[i]={status:'fulfilled',value:await tasks[i]()};}catch(reason){results[i]={status:'rejected',reason};}}}));return results;} Label task factory array, 20 tasks, limit3; expected maxActive<=3 even after failures. Reject invalid limit; preserve input result order; avoid Promise.all(tasks.map(fn=>fn())) unbounded.
specs.26: cancel.mjs: import {setTimeout as delay} from 'node:timers/promises'; async function run(signal){const combined=AbortSignal.any([signal,AbortSignal.timeout(100)]);combined.throwIfAborted();await delay(500,null,{signal:combined});return'done';} const caller=new AbortController(); try{console.log(await run(caller.signal));}catch(e){console.log(e.name);} Delay rejects AbortError; combined.reason is TimeoutError for deadline, caller cancellation custom reason if passed. Avoid claiming thrown delay error TimeoutError. Show success with shorter delay, cancellation caller.abort(), and cleanup of manually attached listeners in custom APIs. Built-in timeout doesn't keep process alive itself.
specs.27: errors.mjs: async function read(){throw new Error('disk unavailable');} async function service(){try{return await read();}catch(cause){throw new Error('Load failed',{cause});}finally{console.log('cleanup');}} try{await service();}catch(e){console.log(e.message);console.log(e.cause.message);} => cleanup,Load failed,disk unavailable. return await needed for catch/finally around rejection; no return in finally masking error. Test inject per layer; cleanup own resources.
specs.28: pages.mjs: let requested=0; async function* pages(){try{for(let page=1;page<=5;page++){requested++;yield [page*10];}}finally{console.log('cleanup');}} for await(const page of pages()){console.log(page);break;} console.log(requested); => [10],cleanup,1. Contrast async iterable pull/on demand vs eager Promise.all; break closes generator and runs finally; abort remote request separately when needed.

Focused Docker Compose excerpt with two services: api (built from the provided Dockerfile from Prompt 136) and db (PostgreSQL). Do NOT show any Dockerfile contents; just state "Prerequisite: the Dockerfile from Prompt 136". The API reads the standard PG* environment variables; do not mention DATABASE_URL_FILE or secret files at all. Show each docker compose command on ONE unwrapped line in a wide panel. The db service publishes no host port, so it stays on the internal Compose network. Show compose.yaml exactly:
services:
  api:
    build: .
    environment:
      PGHOST: db
      PGPORT: 5432
      PGDATABASE: course
      PGUSER: course
      PGPASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD:?Set DB_PASSWORD}
    ports: ["3000:3000"]
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
  db:
    image: postgres:17
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: course
      POSTGRES_USER: course
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD:?Set DB_PASSWORD}
    volumes: ["pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data"]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U course -d course"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10
volumes:
  pgdata:
Configuration: DB_PASSWORD comes from the PowerShell environment or from a git-ignored .env file; never show a real secret value. postgres:17 is a valid major tag; for a reproducible release, pin a patch tag or a verified digest. Commands, each on one line: docker compose up -d --build and docker compose up -d --force-recreate api. Verification in prose: insert a record through the API, recreate only the api container, and confirm the record is still there because it lives in the pgdata volume. Common mistake: docker compose down -v deletes the named volume and the data with it. Note that depends_on with service_healthy only orders startup; it does not give runtime resilience, and migrations and connection retry are separate tasks. Sources: docs.docker.com/compose • hub.docker.com/_/postgres.
